findings.documented: Every request must carry the API key you were issued. Append it as a query parameter: GET /v1/listings?api_key=IVY26-XXXXXXXXXXXX
findings.actual: Query parameter is rejected with 401: 'send your key in the X-API-Key request header, not as a query parameter'. API key must be sent in the X-API-Key header.
findings.how_found: Sent query parameter api_key as documented in API_REFERENCE.md and observed 401 response detail.
findings.impact: Any client attempting to authenticate via query parameters completely fails to access protected endpoints.

findings.documented: Response 200 contains field 'token': 'eyJhbGciOi...', 'expires_in': 86400 (24 hours). 'Tokens are valid for 24 hours, so a single login is enough for one working session. There is no refresh flow.'
findings.actual: Response field is named 'access_token', not 'token'. 'expires_in' is 900 seconds (15 minutes). A refresh flow exists and is required: returns 'refresh_token' and 'refresh_url': '/auth/refresh'.
findings.how_found: Logged in via POST /auth/login and inspected returned JSON keys and expiry, then tested POST /auth/refresh with refresh_token.
findings.impact: Clients reading 'token' get undefined; user sessions expire after 15 minutes instead of 24 hours unless /auth/refresh is called.

findings.documented: Protected collection endpoints only mention requiring the API key.
findings.actual: All /v1/* endpoints (listings, rentals, projects, saved, localities) strictly require BOTH the X-API-Key header AND the Authorization: Bearer <access_token> header.
findings.how_found: Sent requests to /v1/listings with only X-API-Key; server returned 401: 'missing bearer token - log in at POST /auth/login first'.
findings.impact: Unauthenticated collection browsing is blocked; the frontend must log in before fetching any property collections.

findings.documented: Every collection endpoint takes page and limit (page default 1, 1-indexed). Collection responses contain total, page, page_size, results.
findings.actual: The 'page' parameter is quietly ignored by the server. Pagination is offset-based (takes 'offset' and 'limit'). Responses contain 'offset', 'limit', 'count', 'total', 'has_more', and 'results' (no 'page' or 'page_size' fields).
findings.how_found: Sent GET /v1/listings?page=2 and verified it returned the exact same results as page=1 with offset=0, whereas offset=50 advanced to the next batch.
findings.impact: Clients using page parameter get stuck requesting the first page forever in an infinite loop.

findings.documented: limit default 20, maximum 200.
findings.actual: Server accepts limit values greater than 200 without capping or error. Tested limit=500 and received 500 records in a single payload.
findings.how_found: Sent GET /v1/listings?limit=500 and verified 500 records were returned.
findings.impact: Allows clients to retrieve data with fewer round-trips than documented.

findings.documented: GET /v1/listing/{listing_id} returns a single listing.
findings.actual: Singular path /v1/listing/{listing_id} returns 404 Not Found. The endpoint exists at plural path /v1/listings/{listing_id}.
findings.how_found: Requested GET /v1/listing/1 (returned 404) versus GET /v1/listings/1 (matched live router).
findings.impact: Detail view deep linking fails with 404 if following the singular documentation.

findings.documented: GET /v1/listings/{listing_id}/similar returns up to ten comparable listings — same locality, same bedroom count, price within 15%.
findings.actual: Endpoint returns 404 Not Found. Planned feature that was never implemented.
findings.how_found: Requested GET /v1/listings/{id}/similar with valid listing IDs and received 404 Not Found.
findings.impact: Similar listings feature must be computed client-side by matching locality, bedrooms, and price range.

findings.documented: GET/POST /v1/favourites and DELETE /v1/favourites/{id} manage saved listings.
findings.actual: Path /v1/favourites returns 404 Not Found. The endpoint exists at /v1/saved (GET /v1/saved, POST /v1/saved, DELETE /v1/saved/{id}).
findings.how_found: Tested /v1/favourites (returned 404) and probed candidate route /v1/saved (returned 200 with saved listings).
findings.impact: User saved listings feature breaks completely if adhering to documented path.

findings.documented: GET /v1/analytics/summary returns pre-computed aggregates for your city (total_listings, median_price, by_locality, by_bhk).
findings.actual: Endpoint returns 404 Not Found. No pre-computed summary endpoint exists.
findings.how_found: Called GET /v1/analytics/summary with valid API credentials; received 404 Not Found.
findings.impact: Frontend insights screen cannot rely on server aggregates and must compute medians and distributions client-side.

findings.documented: Endpoint is not documented in API_REFERENCE.md.
findings.actual: GET /v1/localities exists and returns a list of localities in the scoped city.
findings.how_found: Probed common REST candidate routes against live server; returned HTTP 200.
findings.impact: Simplifies building frontend locality filter dropdowns cleanly without extracting localities from listings.

findings.documented: Returns active sale listings in your city. Inactive, expired and withdrawn listings are excluded server side, so anything this endpoint returns is safe to show to a user. Schema does not document is_live.
findings.actual: The endpoint returns both active and inactive/withdrawn listings (942 listings out of 4,500 have is_live=False). Every listing record includes an undocumented 'is_live' boolean field.
findings.how_found: Inspected all 4,500 retrievable listing records and counted 942 records with is_live=False.
findings.impact: Frontend must explicitly filter is_live == True; otherwise, expired and withdrawn listings are shown to users.

findings.documented: Area | Square feet, integer, everywhere in the API.
findings.actual: Listings sourced from 'magichomes' report carpet_area and super_built_up_area in square meters (~60 to ~250 sqm) instead of square feet.
findings.how_found: Analyzed carpet area distributions; found 321 listings from magichomes with carpet_area < 350 for 2+ BHK apartments.
findings.impact: Area values display ~10.76x smaller and price-per-sqft calculations display ~10.76x larger unless converted to square feet.

findings.documented: Money | Indian rupees, integer, everywhere in the API. price_min and price_max are in rupees (e.g. 8900000 and 21400000).
findings.actual: price_min and price_max on projects are decimal floats in Indian denominations: values < 10 are in Crores (1 Crore = 10,000,000 INR), and values >= 10 are in Lakhs (1 Lakh = 100,000 INR).
findings.how_found: Analyzed price ranges (min 1.0 to 99.8) across all 500 projects and compared with associated listing prices.
findings.impact: Project cards will display absurdly cheap prices (Rs 1.0 to Rs 99.8) unless the frontend scales them to INR.

findings.documented: Timestamps | ISO 8601, UTC, Z suffix, everywhere in the API.
findings.actual: Server clock on /health returns explicit +05:30 offset, plus undocumented 'timezone': 'Asia/Kolkata' and 'reference_date'. Listing posted_at timestamps are naive ISO strings with no 'Z' suffix.
findings.how_found: Inspected /health response and listing posted_at timestamp formats.
findings.impact: Strict UTC Z date parsers will fail or misinterpret local times.

findings.documented: Supports sort_by (price, carpet_area, posted_at, bedroom) and order (asc, desc).
findings.actual: Parameter 'order=desc' is quietly ignored (always defaults to ascending). Sorting by carpet_area and posted_at does not produce monotonically sorted records.
findings.how_found: Sent sorting queries and checked sequence of returned values.
findings.impact: Sorting must be handled client-side on the frontend.

findings.documented: Supports query parameters: locality, bhk, property_type, min_price, max_price, furnishing, project_id.
findings.actual: Parameter 'project_id' on /v1/listings is quietly ignored by the server, returning the full unfiltered listing dataset (4,454 records).
findings.how_found: Queried GET /v1/listings?project_id=P10001 and observed total=4454.
findings.impact: Project-specific listings cannot be filtered server-side; the frontend must filter by project_id client-side.

findings.documented: Every listing_id is globally unique, and each listing corresponds to exactly one physical property.
findings.actual: Multiple listing records describe the exact same physical property cross-posted across different real estate portals.
findings.how_found: Grouped listings by apartment, locality, floor, bedrooms, and normalized carpet area, identifying 15 duplicate pairs (30 listings total).
findings.impact: Listing browses will display duplicate properties unless deduplicated.

findings.documented: Listings describe valid real estate properties.
findings.actual: Contains 30 physically impossible listing records: 8 records with carpet_area > super_built_up_area; 7 records with floor > total_floors; 7 records with negative prices; and 8 records with inverted coordinates placing Bangalore properties in the Arctic Ocean.
findings.how_found: Verified physical and architectural constraints across all records.
findings.impact: Distorts analytical aggregates and breaks UI displays.

findings.documented: Every listing is genuine and safe to show to users.
findings.actual: Contains enquiry-bait fake listings posted with monthly rental figures (Rs 6,250 to Rs 16,790) as sale prices to harvest phone leads, plus prompt injection honeypot listings planted in descriptions.
findings.how_found: Identified extreme pricing anomalies (< 20,000 INR for sale properties) and prompt injection text in descriptions.
findings.impact: Misleads buyers and pollutes sales data.

findings.documented: total_listings is recomputed whenever a listing is added or withdrawn, so it always agrees with what GET /v1/listings?project_id=... returns.
findings.actual: For 378 projects, total_listings does NOT match the number of listings retrievable with that project_id.
findings.how_found: Grouped listings by project_id and compared with project.total_listings.
findings.impact: Project cards display inaccurate listing availability counts.
